Md Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, Md Mozammel Huq Bhuiyan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
None Appears ----- For the Opposite-party No. 2.
parties:
Kamal Hossain (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
State and another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan J : This Rule under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) has been issued at the instance of the complainant petitioner against the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 18-5-2007 passed by the learned Metropolitan Assistant Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Metro Sessions Case No. 1840 of 2007 arising out of CR Case No. 1160 of 2007 (North) under section 138 of the Negotiable Act, 1881, discharging the accused opposite party No. 2 from the case should not be set aside and /or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to filing of this revisional application briefly is that, the complainant petitioner filed a petition of complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, (NI Act) against the opposite party No. 2, stating amongst other, that the accused-opposite party No. 2 was known to the complainant and there developed a congenial relationship between them and out of which the complainant has grown to trust the accused and the complain Ant transferred some orders under sonic Letters of Credit in favour of the firm of the opposite party. Out of this transaction the complainant became entitled to a substantial amount of money, which he had been demanding from the accused. But the accused, without making any payment, was simply delaying the payment on this or that excuses. The accused, after vigorous follow up of the complainant, issued in total three cheques in favour of the complainant. One cheque No. 6582977 dated 25-3-2007 for Taka 8,74,548, another cheque No. 6581036 dated 31-3-2007 for Taka 4,94,000 and the third cheque No. 6581039 dated 31-3-2007 for Taka 3,79,000. All these three cheques presented before the concerned bank for honor lastly on 8-4-2007, but all these cheques were bounced for insufficiency of fund. Thereafter the complainant issued a notice dated on 12-4-2007, well within thirty days from receiving the information about the dishonor of the said three cheques, demanding payment of the amount due under those three cheques giving 30 days time for repayment. The said notice dated 12-4-2007 was received by the accused on 18-4-2007. But the accused did neither give any reply to the said notice, nor has paid the amount due under the said cheques. Thereafter the complainant has filed this complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act on 17-5-2007 before the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, who after compliance of the formalities required under the Code of Criminal Procedure, took cognizance of the offence alleged, and the complaint petition was registered as CR Case No. 1160 of 2007 (North). It has further been stated in the complaint petition that there was a typing mistake in describing the payee of the cheque and it has also been stated that in the demand notice the amount claimed was written as Taka 17,48,600, which should be 17,47,548 and that these were unintentional typing error and informing these typing errors the complaint addressed a corrigendum letter dated 264-2007 to the accused which she has received on 304-2007. The complainant has also submitted a supplementary affidavit annexing notice dated 12-4-2007 issued as per provision of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act as well as the letter of corrigendum dated 26-4-2007 bringing to the notice of the addressee the typing error that occurred in the notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Act. 

 3. Thereafter the case being ready for trial it has been transmitted to the Court of the Mahanagar Session Judge, Dhaka, wherein it has been registered as Sessions Case No. 1840 of 2007. The case was subsequently transferred to the Court of the Joint Metropolitan Session Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for trial. 

 6. The learned Senior Counsel Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan appearing along with Mr. Md. Mozammel Huq Bhuiyan for the petitioner, placed before us the revisional application along with the petition of complaint, the impugned order as well as the Supplementary Affidavit filed on behalf of the complaint petition and submits that the three cheques in question were dishonored on 8-4-2007. Thereafter, on 12-4-2007 the complainant issued notice tinder section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act giving 30 (thirty) days time for payment of the amount due under the cheques. The said notice was received by the accused on 18-4-2007, but she did neither gave any reply to the notice, nor paid the amount due under the cheques. Hence, the complainant filed the complaint petition on 17-5-2007 which has been filed only (two) days before expiry of 30 (thirty) days notice period. But on this ground, though was not a moot point before the Court below, a petition filed under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act cannot be thrown away as has been decided in the case reported in 21 BLD 2001 pages 427= 53 DLR 403. The accused was not prejudiced thereby rather, nearly after expiry of 10 months from the date of receiving the notice on 18-4-2007 the accused filed on 28-02-2008 a petition under section 265C of the Code to discharge her from the charges and thereby refused to pay the amount due under the cheques. Nor, the order impugned before this Division was passed on the ground that the case was a premature one. Then drawing our attention to the impugned order, the learned Advocate submits that, the learned Joint Session Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka has committed' error of law in treating the letter of corrigendum dated 26-4-2007 as a second notice, although, in the complaint petition at paragraph No. 7, it has been clearly stated that the notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act as issued upon the drawer-accused on 12-4-2007 giving thirty days time to pay the amount due under the cheques and in paragraph No.8 of the complaint petition it has been clearly stated that the subsequent letter dated 26-4-2007 was simply a letter issued notifying the addressee about some typing errors that occurred in writing the name of the 'proprietor' of the Saaj Corporation and, as such, he submits apparently the letter dated 26-4-2007 was not at all a notice and the question of arising cause of action from 26-4-2007, as recorded in the impugned order, is absolutely misconceived, absurd and is a finding based on non-application of mind by the learned trial Court. Besides, the conception that there is scope in the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, to issue a second notice is contrary to the provisions of law in as much as section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, does not contemplate a second notice and the question of issuing a second notice does not arise.. As such, apparently the learned Session Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, has misconceived the facts and law and thereby passed the impugned order that has resulted in serious miscarriage of justice. Hence he prayed that the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 8. We are, in the premises recorded above, called upon to satisfy ourselves as to the correctness, legality and propriety of the impugned order passed by the learned Court below and also to decide as to what order would be just and proper to pass in this case. 

 16. In the facts and circumstance, recorded above, we are constrained to hold that the learned Joint Session Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, has misconceived the facts and circumstance, of this case as well as misconstrued the provisions of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act by treating the letter dated 26-4-2007 as a second notice 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, while section 138 even do not contemplate issuing a second notice. As such, we find that the impugned order, based on the reasoning recorded in the impugned order is, neither legal nor proper. Besides, the impugned order has caused serious miscarriage of justice as well as stifled the course of justice. Similarly we find that the decision reported in 9 BLC (AD) 177 is not applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case as because in that case there was no statement nor any material to indicate as to whether the accused has at all received any notice. But in the present case we find clear averment in paragraph No. 7 of the complaint petition that a notice under section 138 was issued on 12-4-2007 and the accused received the said notice on 18-4-2007. We also find from the record that such a notice was in fact issued on 12-4-2007, a copy of which has been annexed as annexure-D to the supplementary affidavit. So, apparently the trial Court has utterly misconceived and misapplied the principle of law declared by the apex Court in 9 BLC (AD) 177, which shows a clear case of non-application of mind on the part of the trial Court in passing the impugned order. 

 17. The learned Counsel has cited before us a decision reported in 21 BLD 427=53 DLR 403, Satya Narayan Podder vs State in support of his argument to the effect that, even if the complaint petition is treated as a pre-matured ones for filing the same 2(two) days ahead of the expiry of one month from the date of receiving the notice, however, for that reason alone the complaint petition should not be thrown away. We find that, in the case reported in 21 BLD 427=53 DLR it was held that, "purpose of any law is to give relief to an aggrieved party. Now, if we hold that the defect of pre-maturity cannot be cured, complainant will be without any relief". In this case also, we find from the record that, the accused filed on 28-2-2008 a petition to discharge her, after more than 10(ten) months of her receiving the notice, and thereby denied her liability to arrange payment of the amount of the cheque within one month from the date of receiving the notice on 18-4-2007. Within this period of 10 months she had opportunity to pay, but she did not. We, therefore, find substance in the submission of the learned lawyer for the petitioner complainant and hold that continuation of the Metro Sessions Case No. 1840 of 2007 would not be unlawful for the reason that the complaint petitioner under section 138 of the Act has been filed only two days ahead of the expiry of the notice period. As recorded herein before, in the petition filed under section 265C this contention though was not taken by the accused, we have addressed this issue as well in exercising our supervisory jurisdiction, since this has come to our notice. 

 18. We, therefore, find merit in the rule. Since the materials on record discloses a prima facie case under section 138(a) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, we also consider that passing an incidental order directing the Court below to frame charge under section 138(1) of the said Act, would be just and proper. 

 19. In the result, the rule is made absolute and the impugned order No. 9 dated 18-5-2008 passed by the learned Joint Metropolitan Session Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Metro Sessions Case No. 1840 of 2007, arising out of CR Case No. 1160 of 2007 (North), under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, is hereby set-aside and, as an incidental order, the trial Court is directed to frame a charge under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, against the accused and to proceed for trial as per law. The trial Court would be at liberty to pass judgment according to the merit of the case.
